summary.intent: Fix a macOS desktop CI flake (Test 5 cross-client sync failure after file edits) and investigate whether the FUSE-T+SMB architecture could be simplified or unified with Linux.
summary.outcome: PR #558 confirmed green across two independent macOS runs and all platforms; Test 5 now syncs in 35s (was timing out). FUSE-T+SMB architecture research concluded it cannot be replaced with macFUSE due to Apple Silicon kext constraints. Todo for the desktop CI flake was marked completed on a new docs branch.

repo: macFUSE requires a kernel extension (kext) on Apple Silicon, which demands recovery mode to load third-party kexts — not viable for consumer installs; FUSE-T was chosen for this reason, not a bug.

FUSE-T's backend was switched from NFS to SMB due to a macOS Sequoia 15.3 kernel bug where the NFS client never sends WRITE RPCs to FUSE-T's NFS server for newly created files (process hangs permanently); FUSE-T author confirmed and reported to Apple.
FSKit (the Apple-sanctioned kext-less FUSE alternative) is restricted to /Volumes mount points and macOS 15.4+, ruling it out for ~/CipherBox mounts.

drain_refresh_completions gated branch skips populate_folder during local publishes, which suppresses remote-edit re-resolution — this was the root cause of the Test 5 flake and is a pre-existing issue unrelated to Phase 60.

Test 7 (folder rename sync) on macOS uses an optional-warn escape hatch ('FUSE folder rename sync (optional on macOS -- timed out)') so it always 'passes' — the actual rename detection failure is masked in CI results.
The fix mark_remotely_edited_files_unresolved re-resolves genuine remote file edits using strict newer-mtime + same-pointer checks without touching folder structure or local mutations.
workflow: macOS CI job logs must be grepped for 'Sync detected on attempt N' vs 'WARN: FUSE mount did not detect' to distinguish real detection from the optional fallback — job pass/fail alone is insufficient for Test 7.
Todo bookkeeping changes (marking resolved sections) should go on a separate docs branch from the code-fix PR to avoid mixing concerns.
When a fix is deliberately scoped, empirical CI log verification is the reliable way to confirm the fix boundary and rule out side effects on adjacent test cases.

friction: gh API job-id fetch returned a transient empty response, requiring a manual retry before log grepping could proceed.
Test 7 folder rename detection still silently degrades to an optional pass on macOS — the pass/fail signal in CI is misleading without log inspection.
open_items: Test 7 (folder rename sync on macOS): requires a separate, riskier change — structural rename reconciliation while a local publish is pending, which risks clobbering the name_to_ino index; may also be blocked by SMB directory cache TTL regardless.
PR #558 is clean and mergeable but awaiting explicit user approval to merge.
Phase 60 staging wipe + redeploy is unblocked by #558 but not yet initiated.
Worth verifying whether the macOS Sequoia NFS WRITE-RPC bug is fixed on current CI runner macOS versions — would only restore the NFS backend option (likely a lateral move, not an improvement).
